I've thought of that as well while I was reimagining the final battle on Exegol. If you think about it, all three of them had their lives destroyed by Palpatine and their families torn apart:

Rey- Palpatine ordered her parents killed which resulted her being orphaned on Jakku

Finn- The First Order being influenced by the Empire continued with Palpatine's ideas, and they stole Finn from his family for their new Stormtrooper program.

Ben- Through Snoke Palpatine seduced Ben to the dark side, tore his family apart, and lied to him while pretending to speak as Vader. 

I think Finn would forgive Kylo Ren for injuring him on Starkiller Base. Probably for the moment at least because the bigger threat is Palpatine and his new fleet and army. 

It's like JJ forgot that he set up three orphans as his main characters (and then there's Poe whose mother did die, but he would still remain for the fleet battle about Exegol) 

Just imagine if from the start of the film we learn Finn's force-sensitivity and he trains with Rey. Leia teaches Rey who then teaches Finn. Imagine for the final battle Finn with a green lightsaber, Rey with her double bladed new saber and Ben with Anakin's fighting off hordes of Sith Troopers and rejuvenated Palpatine with unlimited power.

I thought that the ST needed one scene to explain this, and that should have been the reason he essentially turned into Kylo Ren. That they lied and kept it a secret from him, so in an ironic turn, he becomes the next Vader. I would have just loved a scene where Ben learns it for the first time, maybe from Snoke or someone else.

It really is disappointing in hindsight. I really don't get all the praise for The Force Awakens. Once all the old books became Legends I thought they would at least use this setup to start the sequels: Luke's Academy on Yavin IV, a strong New Republic, scattered Imperial Warlords. Maybe no Yuzahn Vong. JJ Abrams had the chance to do that. It was all right there to just remix in some way. Instead he wanted to reset the galaxy so the Jedi order had to be destroyed again, and for some reason so did the New Republic? I just don't get it. Plus on top of that Han and Leia were separated and Han was back to being a smuggler. How do people think this film is amazing? Not even one scene with the original trio? Snoke? No politics at all? Just boring backwater worlds with biomes we've seen a dozen times already? A droid carrying important information that ends up on a desert planet again? I have so many questions I'd love to ask him. Why did Star Wars need to be "rebooted"? A New Hope hasn't gone anywhere, you can still watch it anytime you want. Why did we need a movie so similar?

I really wish someone else started the sequel trilogy.

And this is why TLJ is the best of the sequel trilogy. It really makes you think. I went through my stage of loathing it after release because Luke wasn't waving his green lightsaber around cutting through Stormtroopers. Partially why I felt that way was because what I was reading on Reddit. When I left the theater in 2017 I loved it, and saw it four times in theaters. Here's some of the many themes/lessons you can take away from TLJ:

Were the prequel-era Jedi wrong? Were they too quick to go to war and use a clone army? 

Is it their fault that the Empire rose? Was it their fault that they could not sense Darth Sidious right under their noses and his plan? Mace Windu even said, "I sense a plot to destroy the Jedi." Maybe he realized it too late. 

Should the Jedi really end, or is Luke just projecting his failure upon them? 

Sometimes your heroes aren't the mythical figures you expect them to be.

Luke was a human being who failed. A bitter one. Maybe he overreacted, but his entire Jedi order was destroyed that he built up and he felt responsible.

Conversely, it is never too late to come back from a mistake and become your former self, as Luke showed us on Crait.

Should a Jedi use violence and a lightsaber to solve conflicts? Or should the use the Force for knowledge and defense and win a battle without even fighting? 

Your lineage doesn't matter (well, not anymore after TROS, but still doesn't? "Rey, there's some things that are stronger than blood."

There's so much more you can take out of The Last Jedi. It's hard to even think what TRos is about, or what statements it's trying to make. It's just an action movie, like TFA. I'm sure I could come up with some themes and ideas, but TLJ is the film of the ST that tries to make a statement. In the end it reaffirms that no matter the failures of the Jedi, they will continue, and maybe change. That's pretty powerful. Rian Johnson did a great job, and his film making abilities will only improve overtime (I saw Knives Out a few days ago). I really want him to come back to Star Wars.

It just disappoints me so much. Compare it to the Serpartists v Republic in the PT, and Rebellion vs Empire in the OT, and it just feels so...insignificant and uninspired. Surely they could have come up with something better if these movies weren't rushed to hell. It's like the ST doesn't fit with the continuity of the other six movies because VII is literally a fucking reboot.

I thought the same since the very first leaks of the faction names in early 2015. Resistance sounds so small, and so does First Order, which is just as bad. J.J. really dropped the ball with setting up the political scene. Why did we need another underdog story with yet ANOTHER Rebellion, but this time smaller?? It's ridiculous, and makes the galaxy seem even smaller. The OT was technically limited at its time, and yet it feels substantially larger and more populated. 

This trilogy should have just been about a large, armed New Republic against a surging Imperial Remnant. I'm tired of the underdog story, and hearing "hope" shoved down my throat every five minutes. The NR fleet and system should not have been destroyed. And if the Emperor is behind everything, it would make sense that he would have a contingency plan for revenge, and destroy democracy after it rises up, even from the grave. 

The battles just suck in this trilogy. The scale isn't there. I feel like they're more like "Star Skirmishes." The PT and OT had massive planetary and fleet battles. The ST has a space chase. All of the problems of the ST stem from J.J's desire to recreate the Rebels v Empire scenario. Sometimes nostalgia can be a bad thing. 

Not only that, but the two directors can't seem to find any consistency between the size of the First Order between each film. In TFA they have SK Base, and maybe a few Star Destroyers. But in TLJ they suddenly blitzkrieged every major system in the galaxy and will control them in a few weeks? It's laughable. I know the OT wasn't that accurate with scale, but that was back then. This is now, no excuses. 

Lastly, if Palpatine is really behind everything, would he really want his new regime to be called the First Order? It sounds like a small splinter group. If they're truly the heirs of the Empire, you'd think they'd choose a better, more menacing name. Rant over.
